teaching_points.done_well: Uses explicit scale and market reach.

teaching_points.reason: The complete video check found no research, data display, or observable real-result evidence.
teaching_points.missing_or_misused: The one-minute reduction claim has no independent proof presentation.

teaching_points.reason: The complete video check found no explicit second use area beyond the under-eye region.
teaching_points.missing_or_misused: The video stays focused on under-eye concerns.

teaching_points.reason: The complete video check found no named 5D collagen or peptide mechanism linked to an effect direction.
teaching_points.missing_or_misused: Anti-aging is stated as an effect, not explained through the taught ingredient mechanism.

teaching_points.done_well: Pairs a purchase reason with an executable CTA.

storyboard_nodes.reason: The problem list and one-minute result preview make the hook understandable.
Under-eye application is shown, while texture and package presentation are limited.
Millions sold and overseas fame provide concrete social proof.
A one-minute effect is verbally claimed, but no checkable before-and-after or independent result proof is shown.
The complete video check found no clear second use area or daily-life scene.
The complete video check found no 5D collagen or peptide mechanism explanation.
The close provides a value cue and clear shopping-bag action.

relationships.reason: The under-eye problem and result preview lead naturally into product use.
Concrete social proof is present, but the effect claim is not followed by checkable proof.
The complete video check found no proof-to-expanded-benefit transition.
The complete video check found no ingredient mechanism to connect into the CTA.
Attention reaches a purchase action, but effect-proof and mechanism gaps leave major unsupported jumps.
